title: How a CPU adds
subtitle: Five plus three, one gate at a time

scenes.title: Two numbers, as lights
scenes.narration: Inside a computer, a number is a row of wires, each one on or off. Let's add five and three, in four bits.

steps.say: Five is a four plus a one, so the four light and the one light are on.
Three is a two plus a one.
To add them, the computer works like you would on paper: one column at a time, starting from the right.

scenes.title: Adding three bits
scenes.narration: One column adds three bits: the two digits, and a carry from the column before. The answer is at most three, so it fits in two bits, a carry and a sum.

steps.say: Zero plus one is one. Sum one, no carry.
One plus one is two, which in binary is one zero. Sum zero, carry one.
All three on makes three, one one. Sum one, carry one.
Look down the sum. It's on whenever an odd number of inputs are on. That's what an XOR gate does.
The carry is on whenever at least two are on. AND gates can catch that.

scenes.title: One column, in five gates
scenes.narration: Here are those rules as five gates: two XORs, two ANDs and an OR. This circuit is called a full adder.

steps.say: Take the right-hand column: a one on A, a one on B, and no carry in.
The first XOR asks, is exactly one of them on? No, so it outputs zero. The first AND asks, are both on? Yes.
The second XOR mixes in the carry. Zero and zero, so the sum is zero.
And the OR passes the first AND's one out as the carry. One plus one: write zero, carry one.

scenes.title: Four full adders, one per bit
scenes.narration: Now copy that full adder four times, one per column, and wire each carry out into the next column's carry in.

steps.say: Each box is the same five gates we just traced.
The ones column gets one and one. It writes zero, and passes a carry one to its left.
The twos column could not start until that carry arrived. Zero, one and the carry make two again: zero, carry one.
The fours column: one, zero and the carry. Again zero, carry one.
The eights column has only the carry, so it writes one, and nothing carries out.
Each carry had to wait for the one before it, rippling from right to left. That's why this is called a ripple carry adder.

scenes.title: Five plus three
scenes.narration: Read the sum lights from left to right.

steps.say: One zero zero zero. Only the eights light is on, so the answer is eight. Five plus three, done with nothing but on and off.
